name: Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller
notes: The 97-byte report descriptor and the report 0x09 layout are reconstructed from two independent implementations that agree on every field, so no hardware capture was needed: VIIPER's device/ns2pro (descriptor.go item list, inputstate.go buildProReport / proButtonMap / packStick12) and SDL3's SDL_hidapi_switch2.c, the driver SDL routes 057E:2069 to. Three reports are declared. 0x05 is the 63-byte vendor blob a Nintendo protocol host reads, 0x09 is the structured gamepad view, 0x02 is output. Real hardware powers up emitting 0x09 (VIIPER device.go sets activeReportID = ReportIDPro at construction) and switches to 0x05 only when a host sends the subUSBSelectReport subcommand, so 0x09 is what this profile emits and it needs no handshake to be usable. SDL, measured rather than assumed by test/probes/switch2_pro_sdl3_check against an unfiltered SDL3 build with a switch-pro virtual as the same-window positive control. SDL's dedicated switch2 driver is structurally out of reach: HIDAPI_DriverSwitch2_InitUSB needs WinUSB or libusb on the controller's second interface (bulk endpoints on interface 1) and HIDAPI_DriverSwitch2_InitBluetooth is an unimplemented stub upstream that returns 'Nintendo Switch2 controllers not supported over Bluetooth'. A UMDF2 HID profile presents one HID interface and can offer neither, so InitDevice fails. What happens next was the part the withdrawn v1.5.0 asserted without testing: SDL cleans the driver up, the pad falls through to the Windows backend, and it DOES arrive at SDL's joystick layer with 21 buttons and 4 axes. It is not promoted to the gamepad layer, though, because SDL synthesizes mappings only for its HIDAPI, RawInput, WGI and XInput devices and this pad is too new for SDL_gamepad_db.h. The sdlMapping field closes that gap. A consumer prepends the runtime GUID and registers it through SDL_AddGamepadMapping, after which SDL reports a full gamepad including GR, GL and C. Gyro, accelerometer and HD rumble remain unavailable through SDL, since those ride the switch2 driver. GR, GL and C are the Switch 2 additions absent from the original Switch Pro. Headset exists in report 0x05 only and has no bit in 0x09, which is why the descriptor declares 21 buttons plus 3 padding bits rather than 22 plus 2. Sticks are 12-bit, two axes packed into three shared bytes (packStick12), centre 0x0800. The axisMap points leftTrigger and rightTrigger at Z and Ry, usages this descriptor does not declare, because the canonical trigger defaults are Z and Rz and Rz is this pad's right stick Y. Without the map, a consumer pushing the right stick down would also assert ZR. EVIDENCE ASYMMETRY, worth knowing before trusting this blindly: the report 0x05 button map is corroborated by three independent implementations (VIIPER commonButtonMap, SDL HandleSwitchProState, and switch2-controllers-linux ngc/protocol.py SWITCH_BUTTONS), which also explains the 0x10/0x20 gaps in its bytes 0 and 2 as the Joy-Con SR/SL rail buttons a Pro does not have. The report 0x09 map this profile actually emits has ONE source, VIIPER proButtonMap, because the other two consumers parse 0x05. 0x09 is still the right report to emit: 0x05 is an opaque vendor blob in the descriptor and would leave DirectInput and joy.cpl with nothing to read, whereas 0x09 is the structured view that makes the pad usable without any handshake.
